To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the specific binding of EFG to bile canalicular plasma membrane domain from rat liver was first identified.
human epidermal factor (EGF), a growth factor for various cell types, binds to sinusoidal and canalicular membrane domains in rat liver.

the specific binding of human EGF to bile canaliculi membranes isolated from rat livers has been identified for the first times, and the dissociation constant of EGF for bile canaliculi membrane was 2-3 n M, while that for sinusoidal membrane was 4-6 nM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the binding characteristics of EGF to the bile canalicular membrane.

the characterization of specific binding sites for EGF in bile canalicular membranes and the comparison of the binding characteristics between bile canalicular and sinusoidal membranes from the same liver.
the characterization of EGF receptors in liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the specific binding of EFG to bile canalicular plasma membrane domain is a novel finding, but that the specific binding to sinusoidal plasma membranes is not.

EGF binds to both sinusoidal and canalicular membranes of the rat liver with similar dissociation constants, but the binding capacity for the canalicular membrane is about half of that for the sinusoidal membrane.

EGF binding sites are present on the bile canalicular membranes and on the sinusoidal membranes of the hepatocytes, and the number of EGF binding sites is greater on sinusoidal membranes than on bile canalicular membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EGF is a hepatocyte growth factor, and that the EGF receptor is expressed in both sinusoidal and canalicular membranes, but the binding capacity is much greater in sinusoidal membranes.
the binding of EGF was not specific for hepatocytes but was also present in bile canaliculus.
EGF has a specific binding site on bile canalicular membranes and that the binding site is different from those in other membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EGF may play a role in bile formation and/or biliary secretion of other proteins.
EGF binding is not restricted to the sinusoidal domain of hepatocytes but also occurs in the canalicular domain.
EGF binds to the bile canalicular membrane, which is a membrane domain that is not exposed to the blood.
